chunks: 96 - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, he raised it (to the Imams), he said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) leading a group in prayer, and he was in a corner of a room near the wall, and all of them were on his right, and there was no one on his left. And it is not permissible for the one who leads a group in prayer to have his standing place on a surface like a platform or a shop, or something similar to that, and it is permissible for the followers.

97 Narrated - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him about a man who leads a group in prayer while they are in a place lower than his place where he prays, so he said: 'If the Imam is on a surface like a shop or on a place higher than their place, their prayer will not be valid.'

And if he was higher than them by the width of a finger, or more or less, if the elevation from them was by the width of a hand, then if the ground was flat and there was an elevation in one part of it, so the Imam stood in the elevated place and those behind him stood lower than him, and the ground was flat except that they were in a sloping place, he said: 'There is no harm.'

He said: And he was asked: And if the Imam was lower than the place of those praying behind him, he said: 'There is no harm.' And he said: 'And if a man was on a roof or something else like a shop or other than that, and the Imam was praying on the ground lower than him, it was permissible for the man to pray behind him and follow his prayer, even if he was higher than him by a great amount.'

And if two individuals prayed and each one remembered that he was the Imam, their prayers were complete. And if each one remembered that he was the follower, their prayers were invalidated because each one had delegated to his companion the fulfillment of the conditions of prayer, so their prayer was not valid for both.
98 That was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) - from his father (peace be upon him)

He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Regarding two men who differed, one said: 'I was your Imam,' and the other said: 'I was your Imam,' so he said: 'Their prayers are complete.' I said: 'And if each one of them said: I followed you,' he said: 'Then their prayers are invalid, so they should restart.'

And there is no forgetfulness (sahw) on the Imam if those behind him preserved his forgetfulness, and no forgetfulness on those behind him if the Imam preserved their forgetfulness. And if they all doubted, it is obligatory upon them to repeat.
99 Narrated - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him about the Imam who leads four or five individuals, so two glorify (say sahwan) on the basis that they prayed three, and three glorify on the basis that they prayed four, saying: 'These stand up,' and saying: 'These sit down,' and the Imam is leaning with one of them or his doubt is balanced, so what is obligatory upon him?

He said: 'There is no forgetfulness on the Imam if those behind him preserve his forgetfulness with certainty from them, and there is no forgetfulness on those behind the Imam if the Imam did not forget, and there is no forgetfulness in forgetfulness, and there is no forgetfulness in Maghrib and Fajr, and not in the first two rak'ahs of every prayer, and no forgetfulness in a voluntary prayer. And if those behind him differ with the Imam, then upon him and upon them, in precaution, is to repeat and to take the firm position.'
And if the follower forgets the bowing until the Imam enters the second rak'ah, then he should bow and catch up with the Imam, and there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.دُكَّان: Dukkan (shop/stall, used here for elevated surface)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for the Imam's elevation relative to followers in Shia congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elaborates on the spatial hierarchy in congregational prayer, specifying that an Imam standing on an elevated platform (like a *dukkan*) invalidates the followers' prayer, while the reverse is permissible. It further clarifies the mechanics of *sahw* (forgetfulness), establishing that if followers accurately track the Imam's errors, the Imam is exempt from prostrations of forgetfulness, and it resolves the juridical status of two individuals who mutually claim to be the Imam or follow each other.
